mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slow GDP growth combined with high unemployment indicates a weak economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when GDPC1 growth is slow and UNRATE is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing industrial production indicates supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as growth falters.
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when INDPRO growth slows in late-cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as construction and related industries boost economic activity.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of cases when HOUST is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 115 indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as production efficiency and output increase.
failure_condition: If 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of cases when INDPRO exceeds 115, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment and retail sales indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer spending drives growth.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of cases when PAYEMS and RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, increasing federal funds rates lead to negative S&P 500 returns as higher interest rates reduce investment and consumption.
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases in a tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.
